$comment: Fleet-wide enforcement floor. Frontmatter hooks only fire for agents that opt in, so a new
agent added without a `hooks:` block — or the main session — would otherwise run completely
This runs fleet-guard.mjs in `secrets` mode for EVERY tool call in this project: it denies
reading, printing, or exfiltrating .env/.env.* and credential material, and nothing else. The
stricter read-only and writer policies stay in each agent's frontmatter, so ordinary work in
permissions.allow pre-authorises the ship conductor and the GitHub CLI so a shipment runs
without a prompt per step. `gh api --method POST` is deliberately absent: it is the only way
to approve a production deployment or change repo settings directly. Nothing here can deploy
on its own — the `production` environment on GitHub requires a named reviewer.
$autoModeComment: permissions.allow and the auto-mode classifier are two separate gates, and an outward-facing
action has to pass BOTH. `Bash(git push:*)` above was already present when a push was refused
with 'Blocked by classifier': the classifier treats publishing and merging as outward-facing
and does not consult the allow list at all. These rules clear exactly those two cases.
They are written as descriptions rather than command globs because the classifier reasons about
intent, and `gh pr merge --admin` is a different act from `gh pr merge` in a way no glob can
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT COVERED, and still goes through the classifier every time:
- force-pushing or any history rewrite on a shared branch
- `--delete` of a remote ref, and pushing to any remote other than this repo's `origin`
- `--admin` / `--bypass`, i.e. merging past required checks or branch protection
- dispatching a release, deploying, touching the VM, or any destructive database action
The last one matters most: a merge is reversible with a revert, a deploy is not.

allow: Pushing commits or a branch to this repository's own `origin` remote with `git push`, including `-u`/`--set-upstream` on a new branch. Force-pushing, `--delete`, and pushing to any remote other than `origin` are NOT covered by this rule and remain subject to the default rules.
Merging a pull request in this repository with gh pr merge when its required checks have passed, and the branch bookkeeping that follows. Merging with --admin or --bypass is NOT covered.
